teaching.hint: When both sources offer the required next letter, what information distinguishes the possible continuations?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The consumed prefix lengths i and j determine target progress i+j, so no separate target-position dimension is needed.
solution_outline.approach: Check the total lengths. Use a two-prefix reachability table: the final character comes from either source if that character matches the target and its predecessor state is feasible. Keep one row for the memory follow-up.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A state is true exactly when the two specified source prefixes merge into the target prefix of their combined length. In one-row storage, the current entry is the previous row while its left neighbor is the current row.
solution_outline.correctness: Every nonempty valid merge has a final character from exactly one source. Removing it leaves the corresponding smaller prefix state; conversely a matching character appended to any feasible predecessor forms a valid merge. These two exhaustive cases establish the table by induction on i+j. Complete source consumption then decides the requested result.
solution_outline.complexity: O((m+1)(n+1)) time and O(n+1) auxiliary space, with m=|s1| and n=|s2|.
solution_outline.pitfall: A greedy choice when both next characters match can discard the only successful continuation; retain both feasible branches.

common_wrong_turns: A greedy choice when both next characters match can discard the only successful continuation; retain both feasible branches.
source_fidelity_notes: Restated block interleaving as equivalent order-preserving character merge; retained empty strings, complete consumption, length bounds, and the explicit memory follow-up.
